validated_results.title: Dietary lycopene, angiogenesis, and prostate cancer: a prospective study in the prostate-specific antigen era.
validated_results.journal: Journal of the National Cancer Institute
validated_results.reason: This prospective cohort study investigates dietary lycopene intake and incident total and lethal prostate cancer risk with multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios.

extraction.population: US male health professionals aged 40-75 years at baseline in the Health Professionals Follow-up Study

sample_size.excerpt: Among 49898 male health professionals, we obtained dietary information through questionnaires and ascertained total and lethal prostate cancer cases from 1986 through January 31, 2010.

cases.excerpt: Through 2010, there were 5728 total incident prostate cancers and 658 lethal prostate cancers.
cases.location: Methods: Ascertainment and Classification of Prostate Cancer, paragraph 2

effect_size.excerpt: Compared with the bottom quintile, the top quintile of lycopene intake was associated with a hazard ratio of 0.91 (95% CI = 0.84 to 1.00) for total prostate cancer and a hazard ratio of 0.72 (95% CI = 0.56 to 0.94) for lethal prostate cancer. In the time period before the widespread use of PSA screening (before 1994), there was a borderline significant inverse association between lycopene intake and total prostate cancer (top quintile vs bottom quintile: HR = 0.85; 95% CI = 0.72 to 1.00; P trend = .07).

confidence_interval.excerpt: Compared with the bottom quintile, the top quintile of lycopene intake was associated with a hazard ratio of 0.91 (95% CI = 0.84 to 1.00) for total prostate cancer and a hazard ratio of 0.72 (95% CI = 0.56 to 0.94) for lethal prostate cancer.

p_value.excerpt: We found statistically significant inverse associations between quintiles of lycopene intake and incidence of total prostate cancer ( P trend = .009), as well as lethal prostate cancer ( P trend = .04) ( Table 2 ).

comparison.excerpt: Compared with the bottom quintile, the top quintile of lycopene intake was associated with a hazard ratio of 0.91 (95% CI = 0.84 to 1.00) for total prostate cancer

design.excerpt: The Health Professionals Follow-up Study (HPFS) is an ongoing prospective cohort study that consists of 51529 US male health professionals (dentists, optometrists, osteopaths, podiatrists, pharmacists, veterinarians) aged between 40 and 75 years at baseline in 1986.
